story.headline: Australia and China agree to set up an AI dialogue at their annual leaders' meeting in Beijing, days after Australia signed the US-led San Francisco Declaration to secure AI supply chains
story.why: Aus relevance 3/3 (PM-level deal with largest trading partner), debate 3/3 (hedging between Washington and Beijing on AI within one week), measurable 1/2 (joint statement text, 10-country US pact), timeliness 2/2 (+1 under 12h). New development distinct from the 16 Nov (APEC photo) and 17 Nov (US AI pact) packages. COP31 (no final deal yet) and BHP's 13% weekly fall (no company news) scored lower.

linkedin.post:
Two AI deals, one week.

On Friday in Beijing, Anthony Albanese and Premier Li Qiang agreed to establish an AI dialogue "to exchange respective views on AI safety, governance and application", their joint statement says.

Days earlier, Australia was one of 10 countries to sign the US-led San Francisco Declaration to secure AI supply chains.

Albanese says Australia can "manage our differences, but not be defined by them". Analysts point to China's grip on critical minerals refining.

Is Australia smart to talk AI with both Washington and Beijing, or trying to have it both ways?

Tell us what you think below.

#AusSight #auspol #AI

Xi's 'comprehensive turnaround' wording is Reuters' translation; ABC reported it as 'complete turnaround'.
